topic: Anthropic Claude Certified Developer - Foundations (CCDV-F) certification exam preparation
exam_format: 53 multiple-choice and multiple-response questions, 120 minutes, scored 100-1000 with 720 passing, delivered via Pearson VUE (OnVUE online proctored or test center). $125 per attempt; up to 4 attempts per rolling 12 months with escalating waits (14/30/90 days). Credential valid 12 months; on-time renewal is a free non-proctored refresher. Open to individuals - registration is through the Anthropic Partner Academy portal (anyone can join); partner tiers only affect pricing. No mandatory prerequisites; Anthropic recommends 1-5 years software engineering and 6+ months hands-on with Claude or comparable LLM systems, with Python and/or TypeScript.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) with some multiple-response items; heavily scenario-based tradeoff questions
audience: AI engineers, backend developers and technical leads building and shipping production applications, agents and workflows on the Claude platform. Assumes real programming experience (Python/TypeScript) and some LLM exposure; teaches Claude-specific APIs, agents, MCP and optimization patterns in depth.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Applications and Integration
domains.notes: A third of the exam - split across two chapters if needed. Claude API mechanics: Messages API, streaming, tool use, vision, extended thinking, prompt caching, Message Batches API vs realtime (the classic '10,000 documents overnight, cost matters' scenario), Files API. Software engineering foundations: REST, JSON, async patterns, error handling and retries, rate limits. Application design: how Claude behaves differently across Claude Code, Claude Desktop, claude.ai and the raw API. Configuration management: CLAUDE.md files, settings.json, model version pinning. Requirements and lifecycle basics.

domains.name: Model Selection and Optimization
domains.notes: LLM fundamentals as Claude implements them: tokens, context windows, sampling parameters, extended and adaptive thinking. Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku tradeoffs across quality, latency and cost; routing patterns (cheap model first, escalate on need). Token budgeting and cost engineering: prompt caching mechanics (cache writes vs reads), batch discounts, context trimming.

domains.name: Agents and Workflows
domains.notes: Workflow-vs-agent decision making, the agent loop (gather context, act, verify), Claude Agent SDK, subagents for context isolation, orchestration patterns and multi-agent designs, third-party frameworks at awareness level (LangGraph, PydanticAI), long-running agents, human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

domains.name: Prompt and Context Engineering
domains.notes: System prompts as design artifacts, XML-structured prompting, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought and extended thinking prompts, structured output (JSON mode/schemas), context-window management: compaction, summarization, retrieval, what belongs in context vs tools.

domains.name: Tools and MCPs
domains.notes: Designing tool schemas Claude uses reliably, tool-use loop mechanics (tool_use/tool_result blocks), parallel tool calls, when to build a custom tool vs an MCP server vs a skill; Model Context Protocol: server/client architecture, resources vs tools vs prompts, transport options, security considerations of third-party MCP servers.

domains.name: Security and Safety
domains.notes: Prompt injection and jailbreak awareness and mitigations, guardrails and input/output validation, secrets handling around API keys, data privacy in prompts, least-privilege tool design, Anthropic usage policies, safe deployment patterns for agents with real-world side effects.

domains.name: Claude Code
domains.notes: Light coverage to match the 3% weight: what Claude Code is, CLAUDE.md project memory, permissions model, hooks and skills at awareness level, when Claude Code vs the API is the right integration surface.

domains.name: Eval, Testing, and Debugging
domains.notes: Light coverage: eval design basics (golden sets, LLM-as-judge, pass/fail criteria), regression testing prompts, debugging failed tool calls and malformed outputs, observability of agent traces.

extra_guidance: Weights are from the OFFICIAL CCDV-F Exam Guide v1.0 (July 2026) - state them confidently, rounded to whole percents (official figures: 33.1/16.8/14.7/11.0/10.6/8.1/3.1/2.6). Budget chapter time by weight: Applications and Integration deserves 2 chapters; Claude Code and Eval/Testing together can share one lighter chapter. The exam is scenario-first tradeoff judgment, not definition recall - every chapter should drill 'given this constraint, which approach' decisions (batch vs realtime, Opus vs Haiku, workflow vs agent, tool vs MCP server). Use current Anthropic terminology and be accurate about the program: proctored Pearson VUE certification (distinct from free Anthropic Academy course badges), 12-month validity with free on-time renewal, open to individuals via Partner Academy. Recommend the free Anthropic Academy courses (Building with the Claude API, Introduction to MCP, Claude Code in Action) as companion material - positioning this course as the structured exam-prep layer on top. Labs: choose model+caching strategy for a cost scenario, design a tool schema and MCP server split for a use case, sketch an agent loop with a verification step, write an XML-structured system prompt with structured output, and a prompt-injection threat-model exercise. This is a July 2026 exam with almost no prep content anywhere - being early IS the differentiator, so emphasize alignment to Exam Guide v1.0 and commit to updates as the guide iterates. Final chapter must be a full 53-question exam simulation walkthrough with 120-minute pacing strategy and the 720/1000 scaled passing bar.
